bridge_diagnostic.model: lag-2 relative redistribution ~ past performance S_t + current performance S_t+1 + outcome-interval prior size + colony fixed effect
bridge_diagnostic.interpretation: Past performance retains incremental information about t+1 to t+2 redistribution after measured t+1 performance, current group size and persistent colony identity are included.

ecological_interpretation: Relative reproductive performance has weak but detectable one- to two-year memory, so a persistent local-state pathway remains viable. However, past performance still predicts later within-island redistribution after contemporaneous performance, outcome-interval group size and persistent colony identity are included. The leave-one-island-out diagnostic further separates the two signals: removing Torgersen nearly eliminates observed one-year performance memory while leaving the bridge coefficient positive, whereas removing any other single island leaves both coefficients positive. This is consistent with layered dynamics in which persistent local habitat/state effects, especially at terrain-sensitive Torgersen, coexist with a broader short-lived biological memory carried by settlement, retention, breeding dispersal or another unmeasured demographic process.
claim_boundary: Do not claim the persistent local environment has been ruled out.
Do not interpret the bridge model as causal mediation because S_t+1 is post-t.
Do not infer individual public-information use, prospecting, immigration or breeding dispersal from colony counts alone.
The Torgersen leave-one-out pattern is a prespecified sensitivity and is mechanistically suggestive, not proof that snow causes the observed performance autocorrelation.
Direct discrimination among adult retention, breeding dispersal and prospecting requires individual-level mark-resight or tracking data.
